overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of how to form a phenomenologically informed position. You'll be asked about the components of a well-formed position, matching phenomenological concepts to live questions, and telling weak claims from strong ones.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are components of a well-formed position? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: A claim stated so that it could be wrong
options.text: A claim stated so that it could be wrong
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A claim nothing could count against isn't doing any work.

options.html: A statement of what the position doesn't claim
options.text: A statement of what the position doesn't claim
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Scope limits say what the position leaves open.
Correct! Steelmanning meets the strongest objection, not the easiest.

options.html: A complete survey of every view in the literature
options.text: A complete survey of every view in the literature
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A map of positions gives the two or three main answers, not all of them.

options.html: A guarantee that the claim can't be refuted
options.text: A guarantee that the claim can't be refuted
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A good claim is exposed to refutation, not protected from it.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following is the strongest claim for a position statement?

options.html: "Embodiment is probably relevant to consciousness in some way"
options.text: "Embodiment is probably relevant to consciousness in some way"
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. This is so hedged that nothing could count against it.

options.html: "Consciousness is a fascinating and complex topic"
options.text: "Consciousness is a fascinating and complex topic"
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. This isn't a claim about the question at all.

options.html: "No current language model has phenomenal consciousness"
options.text: "No current language model has phenomenal consciousness"
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! It's plain and specific, and evidence or argument could count against it.

options.html: "Some researchers think AI could be conscious"
options.text: "Some researchers think AI could be conscious"
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. This reports others' views. It's a summary, not a position.

forms.stemHtml: Which phenomenological concept is most directly relevant to the question of whether there is a self?

options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The Umwelt bears most directly on animal consciousness.
Correct! Every experience is given as mine, without a separate act of reflection.
Sorry, that's incorrect. That's a clinical finding about disorders of consciousness.
Sorry, that's incorrect. That's a position on AI consciousness, not a phenomenological concept.

forms.stemHtml: What is the term for a claim stated so that some possible evidence or argument could show it to be wrong? Enter two words.

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The test is whether you can say what would count against it.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The term is falsifiable claim.

forms.stemHtml: Why is the Cogitate study a useful model for forming a position?

options.html: It proved global neuronal workspace theory correct
options.text: It proved global neuronal workspace theory correct
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Its results challenged key predictions of both theories.

options.html: It showed that theories of consciousness can't be tested
options.text: It showed that theories of consciousness can't be tested
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. It tested two theories against predictions agreed in advance.

options.html: Its theories stated predictions that could fail
options.text: Its theories stated predictions that could fail
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Because the predictions could fail, the evidence could count against the theories.

options.html: It avoided stating any predictions in advance
options.text: It avoided stating any predictions in advance
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Its predictions were agreed before the data were collected.

title: Forming Your Position
